gold.reasoning: 1. Rheumatoid arthritis–related interstitial lung disease was considered but deemed unlikely — “the same findings plus the absence of a restrictive pattern on pulmonary function tests makes the possibility of rheumatoid arthritis-related interstitial lung disease less likely.” 2. Environmental hypersensitivity pneumonitis was excluded — “There was no history of a recent exposure to hay, dust, or toxic fumes that would suggest these as the underlying cause for our patient’s findings.” 3. Bacterial infection was considered and excluded — “sputum cultures were negative for any bacterial pathogens including acid-fast bacilli… Two sets of blood cultures were negative.” 4. Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis was strongly suspected — “the combination of dyspnea, a history of MTX intake, upper lobe infiltrates on imaging studies and, most important, eosinophilia led us to consider MTX-induced lung toxicity on the top of our differential diagnosis.”

leakage.reason: The patient's own long-term medication; she knows its name. 'Methotrexate' is part of the gold name but the drug history is essential to the case.

source_issues: She denied fever (s002), but her temperature on examination was 38.2 °C (s004).
The examination reports 'mild tachypnea' while the respiratory rate is 16 breaths/min.
Methotrexate 2.5 mg daily for more than 30 years is an unusual regimen; low-dose methotrexate is normally weekly.
notes: Index visit: the presentation with a 1-month history of progressively worsening shortness of breath and nonproductive cough (s001-s013 are this presentation and its workup).
The single denial list in s002 is split into one absent fact per item; hay, dust and toxic fumes are separate exposure facts.
